Navjeevan Shelter Daily Log
Daily Shelter Log

**03:05 – Security Round**
Night guard Pravin completed his hourly round. All exits were secured. No unusual activity. The main gate was found locked as per protocol.

**05:50 – Morning Preparation**
Kitchen staff started the bhandara for breakfast. Menu: poha, tea, and bananas. Water tank levels checked. The overhead tank was at 70% capacity. The borewell pump was started at 06:00 as per schedule.

**06:30 – Day Shift Arrival**
Day shift staff reported for duty. Handover from night shift (Rajesh Kumar) to day shift (Meera Patel) was completed at 06:45. Key points from the handover:
- Generator ran 22:10–23:45 (power cut).
- One medical visit (Ramesh B., headache, paracetamol given).
- No security incidents.
- Occupancy as per night count: 291.

**07:00 – Morning Occupancy Count (Official)**
The official morning headcount was completed. All residents were present in the dormitory areas. Count: 287. The difference from the night count (291) is due to 4 residents who left early for work (they signed out between 05:15 and 06:50). Their names are recorded in the departure register: Sunil P., Manoj K., Dinesh R., and Ashok S. The current occupancy is 287 people as per the morning count. This figure will be used for all official records today.

**07:45 – Breakfast Service**
Breakfast was served from 07:00 to 08:15. Total plates served: 285. Two residents declined breakfast. No complaints about the food. The kitchen staff reported that the tea was slightly over-boiled, but no one complained formally.

**08:30 – Medical Camp Setup**
The visiting doctor's camp was set up in the community hall. Dr. Shah (from the municipal health office) arrived at 08:45. The camp will run from 09:00 to 12:00. Residents were informed via the morning announcement.

**09:15 – Medical Consultations Begin**
First round of consultations started. As of 09:15, 11 residents have been seen. Common complaints:
- Fever (4 cases)
- Joint pain (3 cases)
- Skin rash (2 cases)
- Other (2 cases)

According to the Navjeevan Shelter Daily Log, Navjeevan Shelter current_occupancy is 287 people. Record status: current.

Dr. Shah prescribed medicines for all. The prescriptions were noted in the medical register. The pharmacy stock was checked. We have sufficient paracetamol, ORS, and antacids. We are low on antiseptic cream (only 3 tubes left). Order placed with the supplier.

**10:00 – Maintenance Request**
Resident from dormitory B (bed no. 12) reported a leaking tap in the washbasin area. The tap has been dripping since last night. The maintenance person (Harish) was informed. He will check it after the medical camp. The leak is minor but needs to be fixed to avoid water wastage.

**10:30 – Visitor**
A social worker from a local NGO (name: Kavita Joshi) visited the shelter. She met with the shelter coordinator to discuss a possible skill-training program for residents. She left her contact details. The coordinator will follow up.

**11:20 – Medical Camp Update**
The doctor's camp is ongoing. As of 11:20, 27 residents have been seen. No serious cases. One resident (Maya B., bed no. 45) was advised to get a blood test at the municipal hospital. She was given a referral slip. She will go tomorrow morning.

**12:00 – Medical Camp Closed**
The camp concluded. Total consultations: 31. The doctor left at 12:10. The medical register was updated. Dr. Shah will visit again next Tuesday.

**12:30 – Lunch Preparation**
Kitchen staff started preparing lunch. Menu: dal, rice, sabzi (bhindi), and roti. The cook reported that the gas cylinder pressure is low. We have one spare cylinder. The supplier has been called to replace it. Expected delivery by 15:00.

**13:00 – Lunch Service**
Lunch was served from 13:00 to 14:00. Total plates served: 280. Five residents were not in the shelter during lunch (they had gone out for work or personal errands). They will be served dinner.
**14:00 – Afternoon Count and Rest Period**
Afternoon headcount completed. Total present: 283. Four residents absent (same five who missed lunch, one returned at 13:45). All accounted for. Rest period observed. No incidents reported.

**14:30 – Gas Cylinder Delivery**
Spare cylinder delivered by supplier. Replaced the low-pressure cylinder in the kitchen. Old cylinder marked for return. Kitchen staff confirmed pressure is normal. Cooking for dinner can proceed without interruption.

**15:00 – Maintenance Follow-up (Tap Leak)**
Harish checked the washbasin tap in dormitory B. Replaced the washer. Leak stopped. No further action needed. Recorded in maintenance register.

**15:45 – Generator Check (Routine)**
Daily generator inspection carried out. Ran the generator for 15 minutes as per schedule. Fuel level noted at 40% in the main tank. Two spare jerrycans (20L each) are in storage. Refuelling planned for tomorrow morning.

**16:30 – Evening Tea Service**
Tea and biscuits served in the common hall. Attendance not formally counted; approximately 90 residents present at peak.

**17:15 – New Arrival**
One new resident admitted: Ramesh P., male, age approx. 42. Referred by the railway station outreach team. No visible injuries. He reported that he lost his belongings while travelling and has no local contacts. Allotted bed no. 18 in dormitory A. Basic kit (mat, blanket, toiletries) issued. He was informed of shelter rules and meal timings. He will be registered in the main register by the night supervisor if not completed earlier.

**18:00 – Dinner Preparation Begins**
Kitchen staff started preparing dinner. Menu: dal, rice, roti, and mixed vegetable curry. The five residents who missed lunch will be served dinner first, as noted.

**18:30 – Coordination Call with MMU-7**
Received a call from MMU-7 (mobile medical unit) regarding tomorrow's visit. They confirmed arrival at 09:30 for a routine check-up. They requested that residents who need follow-up (including the blood test referral case) be informed in advance. The night supervisor will make an announcement after dinner.

**19:00 – Evening Count**
Evening headcount completed. Total present: 287. This includes the new arrival. All residents accounted for. No one reported missing.

**19:30 – Dinner Service**
Dinner was served from 19:30 to 20:30. Total plates served: 285. Two residents were not present during service (one had gone to the nearby pharmacy, one was resting and asked for food to be kept aside). Both were served later.

**20:45 – Night Shift Handover**
Day supervisor briefed the night supervisor. Key points:
- New arrival (Ramesh P.) in dormitory A, bed no. 18.
- Medical camp summary: 31 consultations, one referral (Maya B., bed no. 45) for blood test tomorrow at municipal hospital.
- Low stock of antiseptic cream (3 tubes). Order placed; delivery expected in 2-3 days.
- MMU-7 visit confirmed for tomorrow at 09:30.
- Generator fuel at 40%; refuelling planned for tomorrow morning.

**21:00 – Lights Out (Common Areas)**
Common hall lights dimmed. Residents advised to remain in their dormitories. Night supervisor on duty.

**22:15 – Round 1**
Night supervisor did the first round. All dormitories checked. No issues. One resident in dormitory C complained of mild headache. Paracetamol given from the first-aid kit. No further action needed.

**23:30 – Generator Status Check**
Night supervisor checked generator. Running normally. Fuel consumption noted as per the log. No abnormality.

**00:10 – Round 2**
Second round completed. All quiet. No incidents.

**01:30 – Phone Call (Missed)**
A call was received at the shelter office phone at approximately 01:30. The night supervisor was in the dormitory area and could not answer in time. No message was left. The call was not traced. Noted for the morning report.

TIME: 09:15

relay burnt. Also checked pump from top – no obstruction visible. He
suggested pulling the pump out to check impeller/bearing.

documents.title: Navjeevan Shelter Daily Log
documents.content:
**03:05 – Security Round**
Night guard Pravin completed his hourly round. All exits were secured. No unusual activity. The main gate was found locked as per protocol.

**05:50 – Morning Preparation**
Kitchen staff started the bhandara for breakfast. Menu: poha, tea, and bananas. Water tank levels checked. The overhead tank was at 70% capacity. The borewell pump was started at 06:00 as per schedule.

**06:30 – Day Shift Arrival**
Day shift staff reported for duty. Handover from night shift (Rajesh Kumar) to day shift (Meera Patel) was completed at 06:45. Key points from the handover:
- Generator ran 22:10–23:45 (power cut).
- One medical visit (Ramesh B., headache, paracetamol given).
- No security incidents.
- Occupancy as per night count: 291.

**07:00 – Morning Occupancy Count (Official)**
The official morning headcount was completed. All residents were present in the dormitory areas. Count: 287. The difference from the night count (291) is due to 4 residents who left early for work (they signed out between 05:15 and 06:50). Their names are recorded in the departure register: Sunil P., Manoj K., Dinesh R., and Ashok S. The current occupancy is 287 people as per the morning count. This figure will be used for all official records today.

**07:45 – Breakfast Service**
Breakfast was served from 07:00 to 08:15. Total plates served: 285. Two residents declined breakfast. No complaints about the food. The kitchen staff reported that the tea was slightly over-boiled, but no one complained formally.

**08:30 – Medical Camp Setup**
The visiting doctor's camp was set up in the community hall. Dr. Shah (from the municipal health office) arrived at 08:45. The camp will run from 09:00 to 12:00. Residents were informed via the morning announcement.

**09:15 – Medical Consultations Begin**
First round of consultations started. As of 09:15, 11 residents have been seen. Common complaints:
- Fever (4 cases)
- Joint pain (3 cases)
- Skin rash (2 cases)
- Other (2 cases)

According to the Navjeevan Shelter Daily Log, Navjeevan Shelter current_occupancy is 287 people. Record status: current.

Dr. Shah prescribed medicines for all. The prescriptions were noted in the medical register. The pharmacy stock was checked. We have sufficient paracetamol, ORS, and antacids. We are low on antiseptic cream (only 3 tubes left). Order placed with the supplier.

**10:00 – Maintenance Request**
Resident from dormitory B (bed no. 12) reported a leaking tap in the washbasin area. The tap has been dripping since last night. The maintenance person (Harish) was informed. He will check it after the medical camp. The leak is minor but needs to be fixed to avoid water wastage.

**10:30 – Visitor**
A social worker from a local NGO (name: Kavita Joshi) visited the shelter. She met with the shelter coordinator to discuss a possible skill-training program for residents. She left her contact details. The coordinator will follow up.

**11:20 – Medical Camp Update**
The doctor's camp is ongoing. As of 11:20, 27 residents have been seen. No serious cases. One resident (Maya B., bed no. 45) was advised to get a blood test at the municipal hospital. She was given a referral slip. She will go tomorrow morning.

**12:00 – Medical Camp Closed**
The camp concluded. Total consultations: 31. The doctor left at 12:10. The medical register was updated. Dr. Shah will visit again next Tuesday.

**12:30 – Lunch Preparation**
Kitchen staff started preparing lunch. Menu: dal, rice, sabzi (bhindi), and roti. The cook reported that the gas cylinder pressure is low. We have one spare cylinder. The supplier has been called to replace it. Expected delivery by 15:00.

**13:00 – Lunch Service**
Lunch was served from 13:00 to 14:00. Total plates served: 280. Five residents were not in the shelter during lunch (they had gone out for work or personal errands). They will be served dinner.

documents.title: Navjeevan Shelter Daily Log
documents.content:
**14:00 – Afternoon Count and Rest Period**
Afternoon headcount completed. Total present: 283. Four residents absent (same five who missed lunch, one returned at 13:45). All accounted for. Rest period observed. No incidents reported.

**14:30 – Gas Cylinder Delivery**
Spare cylinder delivered by supplier. Replaced the low-pressure cylinder in the kitchen. Old cylinder marked for return. Kitchen staff confirmed pressure is normal. Cooking for dinner can proceed without interruption.

**15:00 – Maintenance Follow-up (Tap Leak)**
Harish checked the washbasin tap in dormitory B. Replaced the washer. Leak stopped. No further action needed. Recorded in maintenance register.

**15:45 – Generator Check (Routine)**
Daily generator inspection carried out. Ran the generator for 15 minutes as per schedule. Fuel level noted at 40% in the main tank. Two spare jerrycans (20L each) are in storage. Refuelling planned for tomorrow morning.

**16:30 – Evening Tea Service**
Tea and biscuits served in the common hall. Attendance not formally counted; approximately 90 residents present at peak.

**17:15 – New Arrival**
One new resident admitted: Ramesh P., male, age approx. 42. Referred by the railway station outreach team. No visible injuries. He reported that he lost his belongings while travelling and has no local contacts. Allotted bed no. 18 in dormitory A. Basic kit (mat, blanket, toiletries) issued. He was informed of shelter rules and meal timings. He will be registered in the main register by the night supervisor if not completed earlier.

**18:00 – Dinner Preparation Begins**
Kitchen staff started preparing dinner. Menu: dal, rice, roti, and mixed vegetable curry. The five residents who missed lunch will be served dinner first, as noted.

**18:30 – Coordination Call with MMU-7**
Received a call from MMU-7 (mobile medical unit) regarding tomorrow's visit. They confirmed arrival at 09:30 for a routine check-up. They requested that residents who need follow-up (including the blood test referral case) be informed in advance. The night supervisor will make an announcement after dinner.

**19:00 – Evening Count**
Evening headcount completed. Total present: 287. This includes the new arrival. All residents accounted for. No one reported missing.

**19:30 – Dinner Service**
Dinner was served from 19:30 to 20:30. Total plates served: 285. Two residents were not present during service (one had gone to the nearby pharmacy, one was resting and asked for food to be kept aside). Both were served later.

**20:45 – Night Shift Handover**
Day supervisor briefed the night supervisor. Key points:
- New arrival (Ramesh P.) in dormitory A, bed no. 18.
- Medical camp summary: 31 consultations, one referral (Maya B., bed no. 45) for blood test tomorrow at municipal hospital.
- Low stock of antiseptic cream (3 tubes). Order placed; delivery expected in 2-3 days.
- MMU-7 visit confirmed for tomorrow at 09:30.
- Generator fuel at 40%; refuelling planned for tomorrow morning.

**21:00 – Lights Out (Common Areas)**
Common hall lights dimmed. Residents advised to remain in their dormitories. Night supervisor on duty.

**22:15 – Round 1**
Night supervisor did the first round. All dormitories checked. No issues. One resident in dormitory C complained of mild headache. Paracetamol given from the first-aid kit. No further action needed.

**23:30 – Generator Status Check**
Night supervisor checked generator. Running normally. Fuel consumption noted as per the log. No abnormality.

**00:10 – Round 2**
Second round completed. All quiet. No incidents.

**01:30 – Phone Call (Missed)**
A call was received at the shelter office phone at approximately 01:30. The night supervisor was in the dormitory area and could not answer in time. No message was left. The call was not traced. Noted for the morning report.

documents.content:
TIME: 09:15
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3 (Submersible pump, borewell)
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Duty staff reported no water pressure in overhead tank
from 06:30 hrs. Checked panel board – pump starter showing overload trip.
Reset the starter once at 09:05, pump ran for approx. 2 minutes then tripped
again. Motor winding continuity checked with multimeter – reading OK (no
short). Suspect mechanical jam or worn bearing.
ACTION TAKEN: Kept pump out of service. Tagged "DO NOT START" on panel.
Drained remaining water from overhead tank to ground storage for kitchen
use. Informed SSN logistics office by phone (call logged by Mr. Desai).
REPORTED TO: Rajesh Kumar, Facility Supervisor (on phone)
SIGNATURE: (illegible) / M. Patel, Maintenance Staff

TIME: 14:30
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3 (Submersible pump)
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: SSN logistics sent electrician (Mr. Iqbal Shaikh) to
check pump. He opened the starter and checked all contactors, found one
relay burnt. Also checked pump from top – no obstruction visible. He
suggested pulling the pump out to check impeller/bearing.
ACTION TAKEN: Relay ordered from Surat electrical shop (M/s Jay Ambe
Electricals). Expected delivery tomorrow morning. Pump not started.
REPORTED TO: Sunita Rao (SSN office) – informed by phone at 15:05
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

----------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 19/07/2024
----------------------------------------------------------------------

TIME: 08:45
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Mr. Iqbal Shaikh arrived at 08:30 with relay. Fitted
relay in starter, reset overload. Started pump – ran for about 1 minute,
then tripped again. Overload relay showing high current (reading approx.
9.5 A, normal is 6.8 A). Motor drawing more current than rated.
ACTION TAKEN: Stopped pump. Mr. Shaikh suspects bearing seizure or
impeller damage. He has arranged for pump pulling – need crane/chain
pulley arrangement. SSN logistics to arrange. Water supply from ground
storage continued; kitchen and bathrooms using stored water only.
REPORTED TO: Rajesh Kumar (in person)
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

TIME: 16:20
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Crane arrangement not available today. Mr. Shaikh tried
to check pump from top only – no conclusion. He has left a note that the
pump must be pulled out. Ground storage level is going down – approx.
4000 litres remaining. Daily consumption approx. 6000 litres. We may face
water shortage by tomorrow evening if pump not fixed.
ACTION TAKEN: Requested SSN to arrange tanker water supply for tomorrow
morning as backup. Also requested urgent crane arrangement.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar (Facility Supervisor)

The Asha Kiran Maintenance Log records Asha Kiran Shelter water_pump_status as nonfunctional. Record status: current.

TIME: 07:30
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: No crane yet. Tanker water arrived at 07:00 (supplier:
M/s Ganga Water Suppliers, 6000 litres). Ground storage refilled.
ACTION TAKEN: Tanker water logged in water register. Pump still out of
service. Mr. Shaikh informed – he will try to arrange a pulley tripod from
another site.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

TIME: 12:10
EQUIPMENT ID: P-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Mr. Shaikh arrived with a tripod and chain pulley.
Pump pulled out at 11:45. Found impeller partially choked with mud and
small stones. Also bearing (bottom) is worn – shaft has play. This is the

sheet. Borewell pipe kept open, covered with wooden plank. No one allowed
near the borewell. Water supply from tanker only.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel / R. Kumar (witnessed)

DATE: 25/07/2024

TIME: 08:15
EQUIPMENT ID: GEN-1
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Morning check of diesel generator. Oil level at 3/4 on dipstick. Coolant level normal. Battery voltage 12.6 V before start. No fuel leak observed around the day tank. Ran the generator on no-load for 10 minutes as per weekly schedule. No abnormal vibration. Auto changeover panel showing normal indication.
ACTION TAKEN: Logged. No action required.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar

TIME: 09:00
EQUIPMENT ID: LTG-2
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: One tube light in the women's dormitory (block B, room 14) not working since last night. Residents reported at 08:45. Checked the fitting – tube appears blackened at one end. Starter also looks old.
ACTION TAKEN: Replaced tube light (Philips 36W, taken from store) and starter. Light working. Old tube and starter disposed in scrap bin. Store issue slip no. 42.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

TIME: 11:30
EQUIPMENT ID: AC-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Air conditioner in the medical room cooling less than usual. Complaints from the visiting doctor. Checked the air filter – found dusty. Also checked the temperature difference across the indoor unit – only 6 degrees, normally it is around 10-11 degrees.
ACTION TAKEN: Removed and washed the air filter. Reinstalled after drying. Will check temperature difference again in the evening. If still low, will contact SSN for refrigerant top-up.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar

TIME: 13:45
EQUIPMENT ID: GEN-1
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: SSN office called. They asked about the generator service schedule. Informed them that the last service was done on 10/07/2024 and the next one is due in the first week of August. They asked if we need the service agency to also check the AMF panel. Told them yes, as the panel had a minor issue last month with the relay. They said they will coordinate with the agency.
ACTION TAKEN: Noted in the maintenance file. Will follow up on 01/08/2024 if no confirmation received.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

TIME: 16:00
EQUIPMENT ID: WTR-2
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Routine inspection of the overhead tank float valve. Tank level was at 80%. Float movement smooth, no sticking. No water overflow from the overflow pipe. Valve stem showing slight rust but not affecting operation.
ACTION TAKEN: Applied a light coat of oil on the float valve stem. Noted for replacement during next annual maintenance.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar

TIME: 18:30
EQUIPMENT ID: LTG-1
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Street light pole no. 3 near the entrance gate not switching on. Checked the photocell sensor – the sensor is not responding to a cloth cover test. The bulb itself is fine as it lights when manually switched on.
ACTION TAKEN: Replaced the photocell sensor with a new one from store. Light working normally. Old sensor kept in store for possible repair by SSN. Store issue slip no. 43.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar

TIME: 20:00
EQUIPMENT ID: GEN-1
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Evening check. Generator not running as there was no power cut today. Checked battery voltage – 12.8 V. Oil and coolant levels normal. Day tank fuel level at 60%. No leaks. Ran the generator for 5 minutes as per routine to ensure it starts properly. Started on first attempt.
ACTION TAKEN: Logged. No action required.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

----------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 26/07/2024
----------------------------------------------------------------------

TIME: 08:30
EQUIPMENT ID: AC-3
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Morning check of the medical room air conditioner. Temperature difference now 10 degrees. Cooling is normal. No complaints from the doctor or staff.
ACTION TAKEN: Logged. No action required.
SIGNATURE: M. Patel

TIME: 09:45
EQUIPMENT ID: WTR-1
ISSUE DESCRIPTION: Complaints from block C that water pressure is low in the morning taps. Checked the main line pressure gauge – showing 1.2 kg/cm2, which is normal. Checked the individual tap in block C – the tap filter is clogged with sand particles.
ACTION TAKEN: Cleaned the tap filter in the common bathroom of block C. Pressure restored. Will check if this repeats – if yes, will inspect the main line for sediment.
SIGNATURE: R. Kumar
